description: If the grading service writes account and parent-child link records without strong audit trails, it may be impossible to prove which process instance or actor initiated a creation or modification. This can hinder accountability for privacy-relevant changes to family relationship data.
assumptions: Write operations may lack tamper-evident logging, request provenance, or signed transaction records.
uncertainty_note: Applies if accountability controls are weak; not certain from the flow description alone.

title: Detectability of family relationships from directory write patterns or stored metadata
description: The existence of parent-child relationship entries in the account directory may allow an observer with access to the datastore, logs, or metadata to detect that a given student has an associated parent account, even without reading full record contents. Presence, timing, or structure of writes can reveal sensitive facts.
assumptions: Attackers or unauthorized insiders can observe directory contents, metadata, or write events.
uncertainty_note: Threat depends on visibility of metadata or record existence; exact subtree node is approximate.

title: Disclosure of sensitive relationship data in the account directory
description: Parent-child relationship links and account records written to the directory may disclose personal data to unauthorized parties if access controls, segregation, or encryption are insufficient. Family relationship information can be especially sensitive because it reveals household structure and associations.

This undermines transparency about what data is stored and how it is reused.

title: Non-compliant storage of relationship data beyond necessity
description: Writing parent-child relationship links into the account directory may violate data minimization, purpose limitation, retention, or lawful-basis requirements if the directory stores more relationship data than necessary for grading or retains it longer than justified. Centralizing family links can also create compliance obligations for special handling and access governance.
assumptions: The directory may serve broader identity purposes than grading, and retention/purpose constraints for relationship data may not be explicitly enforced.

This may disclose more personal data than is strictly necessary for backup/hosting purposes, especially if full records, historical grades, and directory attributes are replicated without minimization, filtering, or segregation.

Sending complete datasets across the trust boundary creates a risk of avoidable disclosure of sensitive personal data categories or high-impact profile information to the third party.

title: Cross-dataset linkability enabled by consolidated backup payload
description: Combining full grade records, assignments, and the account directory in one replicated backup enables the cloud provider, or anyone with access there, to link academic performance, coursework, and identity/account information for the same individuals. This aggregation increases the ability to correlate records across contexts and time.
assumptions: Assumes the replicated datasets contain stable identifiers or quasi-identifiers that permit correlation across the included data domains.

title: Identifiability of individuals in replicated backups

description: The grading service reads the same grade records to build student, parent, and teacher views. description: Students and possibly parents may be unaware that the same underlying grade records are read and repurposed by the service to construct multiple audience-specific views. Without clear notice, users may not understand who can see which parts of the record and under what conditions.
